public_rationale: The claim is that, as of April 2024, adding visual data to LLMs had not solved hallucinations. OpenAI's system card for GPT-4V, dated 25 September 2023, says the model 'was prone to hallucinations' and sometimes made factual errors in an authoritative tone (e1). HallusionBench, accepted to CVPR 2024, tested 15 vision-language models, including GPT-4V, Gemini Pro Vision and Claude 3, in a version dated 25 March 2024. GPT-4V scored highest, with 31.42% question-pair accuracy, and all other models scored below 16%. The paper names language hallucination as one of the failure modes it observed (e2). Both sources fall within the target period, April 2023 to 15 April 2024. Together they show that leading multimodal LLMs still hallucinated in material ways, which meets the support condition. A survey posted on 29 April 2024, after the period ended, says multimodal LLMs often produce hallucinations (e3). It is context only.
limitations: 'Solved' is not defined. The claim is read as hallucinations remaining a material problem, not as adding vision bringing no improvement at all. The evidence packet notes that the GPT-4V system card reports fewer hallucinations during a beta, but that passage is not in the cited excerpt.
HallusionBench reports question-pair accuracy on a set of 346 images and 1,129 questions written by experts. It does not measure how often hallucinations happen in everyday use.
The evidence covers a small number of sources. It does not show how often every multimodal model released in the period hallucinated.

from_speaker: stated in April 2024, looking back on the year since TED 2023
our_interpretation: Plain reading: the multimodal (vision-plus-language) models released between TED 2023 and the post, such as GPT-4V, Gemini Pro Vision and Claude 3, still produced hallucinations often enough to be a recognized, documented problem.

'Solved' means hallucinations were no longer a material problem. Showing that leading models still hallucinated in documented evaluations is enough to support the claim. The claim does not say visual data made no improvement at all.
Target period: from TED 2023 (April 2023) to the post date (2024-04-15).
criteria.support_condition: Developer documentation or published evaluations from the period show that leading multimodal LLMs still hallucinated in material ways.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence from the period shows that leading multimodal LLMs had essentially eliminated hallucinations, or that adding vision had been shown to resolve them.
